articles.title: Variant Foramina of the Orbital Apex: Osteological Evaluation and Systematic Review.
articles.authors: Cezar Octavian Morosanu, Amy Manson, Mae Hunter et al.
articles.abstract: The orbital apex contains several anatomical variations that can significantly impact surgical procedures involving the orbit and skull base. Among these anatomical variants, the metoptic canal (MC), Warwick's foramen (WF), and optic canal duplication (OCD) may serve as important conduits for neurovascular elements. Despite their clinical relevance, these variant structures are inconsistently described in the literature, and data on their incidence and morphology remain limited. This study aimed to investigate the prevalence, morphology, and anatomical relationships of these accessory orbital foramina. A total of 110 adult dry skulls and 15 isolated sphenoid bones from the department of human anatomy were examined. The size, shape, and position of any MCs, WF, or OCDs present were recorded. Morphometric assessments were performed on these foramina as well as the optic canal, optic strut, and superior orbital fissure. A systematic review of relevant studies was also conducted for comparative analysis. Accessory orbital foramina were identified in 20 of the 125 specimens (17.6%). OCD was present in five cases (4%), MC in eleven cases (8.8%), and WF in eight cases (6.4%). Statistical analysis revealed that the optic strut and superior orbital fissure were significantly wider in skulls displaying OCD. In addition, orbits with WF were associated with shorter superior orbital fissures compared to non-variant orbits. The systematic review identified 35 relevant studies for analysis. This study highlights the considerable anatomical variability of accessory orbital foramina and the need for awareness during surgical dissection. Features such as increased size of the optic strut and reduced size of the superior orbital fissure can raise the suspicion of a variant foramen in the orbital apex.

articles.title: Superficial facial musculature in naked mole-rats: Adaptations to a subterranean niche.
articles.authors: Mikaela D Thurber, Diana K Sarko
articles.abstract: Naked mole-rats (Heterocephalus glaber) are eusocial rodents with unusually long lifespans. Adaptations to their subterranean habitat include large, well-innervated incisors used for digging underground tunnel systems; oral folds that close behind the incisors; and a specialized tactile system (sensitive incisors in addition to tactile hairs that cover the entire body). This well-developed tactile system compensates for their reduced visual and auditory systems. Naked mole-rats are functionally blind and have small eyes, even compared to other African mole-rat species. They also have relatively poor auditory capabilities as well as absent pinnae. Although few studies have characterized the facial musculature of naked mole-rats, their facial musculature would be expected to have evolved commensurately with adaptations to a subterranean niche. To examine this, we performed detailed dissections of superficial facial musculature in adult naked mole-rats. This included muscle identification and characterization of attachment sites compared to what has previously been shown in rats. Our dissections demonstrated reduced musculature associated with the eyes (e.g., orbicularis oculi), the ears (e.g., auricularis posterior and interscutularis muscles), and the dorsal head (frontalis and occipitalis muscles), but well-developed musculature facilitating movements of the nose and mouth, befitting the roles of these anatomical structures in sensory perception and social interactions. Our findings not only provide insights into the evolutionary adaptations of naked mole-rat facial musculature to a subterranean niche, but will also help inform future studies assessing and interpreting social-emotional communication in naked mole-rats through the lens of species-specific adaptations in the musculature underlying facial expressions.

articles.title: BoneNet: a framework for predicting MSK-FE-estimated femoral neck strain patterns from exercise IMU data.
articles.authors: Zainab Altai, David Hollinger, Andrew T M Phillips et al.
articles.abstract: Femoral neck fractures pose serious risks, particularly in osteoporosis, highlighting the need for effective bone-strengthening exercises and practical, non-invasive assessment of femoral loading. This study quantifies exercise-induced strains and presents BoneNet, an explainable convolutional neural network that predicts femoral neck strains from inertial measurement unit (IMU) data, offering a potential approach for estimating musculoskeletal-finite element (MSK-FE)-derived femoral neck strain patterns. Data were collected from 40 healthy participants (40.3 ± 13.1 years), with 37 included in the FE and BoneNet analyses. MSK-FE models estimated femoral neck strains during walking, running, jumping and hopping at varying intensities. BoneNet used IMU accelerometer and gyroscope signals from seven- and three-sensor configurations with participant-grouped cross-validation. Fast running yielded 3731 ± 1472 µε (tensile) and - 9541 ± 3610 µε (compressive), with walking strain magnitudes 47% lower for both tensile and compressive strains. Unilateral hopping with longer ground contact yielded 3003 ± 1189 µε and - 7755 ± 3040 µε, with walking strain magnitudes 34% and 35% lower, respectively. Walking generally produced higher strains than all other exercises. Using seven IMUs, BoneNet achieved correlations of r = 0.75-0.94 for five exercises, while squat jumps showed weak correlations (r = 0.27-0.36) and high relative RMSE (54.9-59.4%). Three IMUs showed comparable correlations, but squat-jump errors remained high (relative RMSE 56.0-61.2%). Running at all intensities and unilateral hopping with longer ground contact may have implications for bone adaptation, while BoneNet shows potential for estimating strain patterns rather than validated absolute values.

articles.title: State-space dynamics of joint coordination reveal preserved directional structure across running speeds.
articles.authors: Alessandro Garofolini, William Anthony Sparrow, Rezaul Begg
articles.abstract: Understanding whether locomotor demands are accommodated by reorganising inter-joint coordination or by scaling an existing coordination pattern is a fundamental question in biomechanics and motor control. We examined whether the directional organisation of ankle-knee moment coordination is preserved across running speeds using a state-space representation of their continuous interaction. Sagittal-plane ankle and knee moments were analysed in 31 experienced runners (30 male, 1 female; 28 competitive and 3 elite) running at 2.5, 3.5, and 4.5 m·s-1. Trajectory geometry was characterised by loop area, path length, major-axis orientation, and anisotropy, while trajectory-attached vectors quantified the magnitude and direction of progression through four intrinsically defined coordination segments: Loading, Transfer, Propulsion, and Release. Increasing speed markedly expanded the coordination trajectory, increasing loop area and path length (both p < 0.001), with smaller changes in major-axis orientation (p = 0.003) and anisotropy (p = 0.005). Progression magnitude also increased with speed (p < 0.001), with a Speed × Segment interaction showing that the magnitude of this increase differed across coordination segments (p = 0.006). In contrast, although vector direction showed a significant effect of speed (p = 0.0016), reflecting modest overall directional shifts, but no significant Speed × Segment interaction (p = 0.084): the characteristic directional sequence through Loading, Transfer, Propulsion, and Release was preserved. Thus, running faster scales ankle-knee mechanical coordination while the segment-dependent directional structure was largely preserved. These findings distinguish increased mechanical demand from a clear reorganisation of inter-joint mechanical coordination across running speeds.

articles.title: Neurocognitive Alterations Manifested as Reaction Time Deficits Following ACL Reconstruction: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Observational Studies.
articles.authors: Mostafa Jalili Bafrouei, Manouchehr Moradi Sabzevar, Hooman Minoonejad et al.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction (ACLR) is associated with changes in cognitive-motor processing that may persist beyond physical recovery and are not fully identified by conventional physical performance assessments. OBJECTIVE: This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate neurocognitive function as expressed through cognitive-motor performance following ACLR compared with healthy individuals, with particular emphasis on reaction time and higher-order cognitive outcomes. METHODS: Four databases (PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, Embase) were searched from inception to December 2025. Eligibility criteria included observational studies on cognitive-motor outcomes in individuals from ACLR recovery and healthy controls. Data extraction followed Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 guidelines. Methodological quality was evaluated using the Joanna Briggs Institute appraisal tools. Random-effects models were used to calculate standardized mean differences with 95% confidence intervals. Heterogeneity was assessed with I2, subgroup analyses and publication bias evaluations. RESULTS: Twenty-one non-randomised studies involving 986 participants Twenty-one non-randomised studies involving 986 participantswere included. Neurocognitive performance showed a significant impairment in reaction time from ACLR recovery with a moderate effect size (standardized mean difference = 0.56, 95% confidence interval 0.41-0.71, p < 0.001) and high heterogeneity (I2 = 78%). In contrast, pooled analyses showed no statistically significant differences for error rate, accuracy, visual memory, or visual motor speed. CONCLUSIONS: Anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction is associated with persistent reaction time deficits, whereas pooled analyses of error rate, accuracy, visual memory, and visual motor speed did not demonstrate statistically significant differences compared with healthy controls. This pattern suggests selective impairment in the temporal efficiency of cognitive-motor processing rather than generalized cognitive dysfunction. Reaction time may represent a potential marker of altered cognitive-motor processing following ACLR; however, prospective studies are needed to determine its prognostic value and clinical utility for post-ACLR assessment and return-to-sport decision making.

articles.title: A randomized cross-over comparison of cardiovascular responses to forearm and upper arm post-exercise circulatory occlusion.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: The metaboreflex is often studied using post-exercise circulatory occlusion (PECO) of the arm after handgrip (HG) exercise; however, the location of the occlusion cuff has varied (i.e. upper arm vs. forearm). These variations include differing amounts of muscle tissue which in turn could affect hemodynamic and autonomic responses to metaboreflex activation. Further, recent work has suggested the importance of considering muscle strength when investigating the metaboreflex. Thus, the purpose of the current study was to compare the hemodynamic responses to PECO at two different occlusion sites while measuring indices of metabolite production and concurrently controlling for differences in maximal HG force (max HG) in males and females. METHODS: We recruited 20 young healthy participants (10 female) to complete 2 randomized trials of 2 min of HG at 40% maximal voluntary contraction followed by 3 min of PECO at either the upper arm or forearm. We measured blood pressure, heart rate, oxygenation of the wrist dorsiflexor muscles and blood lactate from the finger. RESULTS: After controlling for max HG, we found that there was a relationship between max HG and the heart rate response to PECO (p = 0.014), regardless of biological sex, without a difference between occlusion sites (p = 0.51). Further, there was no effect of sex, max HG, or occlusion site on mean arterial pressure (p > 0.06), deoxygenation (p > 0.32) or lactate production (p > 0.07). CONCLUSION: Our results indicate that researchers should consider controlling for maximal HG when investigating the metaboreflex, and that responses to upper arm and forearm occlusion after HG exercise elicit responses that are not different.

articles.title: Exercise and insulin independently stimulate galactose uptake into human skeletal muscle.
articles.authors: Thien Vinh Luong, Mette Glavind Bülow Pedersen, Christian Thorup et al.
articles.abstract: Carbohydrate choice affects glycaemic responses during and after exercise, particularly for individuals with impaired glucose regulation. Galactose causes smaller glycaemic excursions than glucose but is thought to require hepatic conversion to glucose via the Leloir pathway before peripheral use. Whether galactose is directly taken up by skeletal muscle, and whether this is regulated by exercise and insulin remains unclear. In this randomised, controlled crossover trial, eight healthy men (age 68 ± 4 years; body mass index 24.7 ± 2.1 kg/m2) completed two 4 h study days, with and without a hyperinsulinaemic-euglycaemic clamp (1.0 mU/kg/min). Galactose turnover was assessed using a primed-constant galactose infusion. Participants performed one-legged, high-intensity knee-extension exercise at maximal capacity, with the contralateral leg as a non-exercised control. Skeletal muscle galactose uptake was quantified by dynamic [1 8F]FDGal positron emission tomography (PET), and arteriovenous (AV) exchange across the leg was determined from femoral blood samples combined with [1 5O]H2O PET-measured leg perfusion. Exercise and insulin markedly increased galactose uptake (exercise effect: P < 0.001; insulin effect: P < 0.001; interaction: P = 0.0769). PET analysis showed that exercise primarily increased tracer influx (K1), while insulin increased intracellular trapping (k3) and modestly reduced efflux (k2). Plasma galactose concentrations were low (0.2 ± 0.1 mmol/L) and galactose AV exchange across the leg did not differ across conditions. Human skeletal muscle can directly take up galactose, and this is stimulated by exercise and insulin. This challenges the assumption that hepatic conversion is required before peripheral utilisation. Future studies should determine whether galactose is incorporated into skeletal muscle glycogen to a physiologically relevant extent. KEY POINTS: Galactose causes smaller spikes in blood sugar than glucose, and it has long been assumed that the body must first convert galactose into glucose in the liver before peripheral use. Using positron emission tomography imaging with the galactose analogue 2-[1 8F]fluoro-2-deoxygalactose in combination with a one-legged knee-extension ergometer, we demonstrated that human skeletal muscle can directly take up galactose. Both exercise and insulin markedly increased skeletal muscle galactose uptake, with an additive effect when combined. Exercise primarily increased galactose uptake by enhancing muscle blood flow, whereas insulin exerted its effect by promoting phosphorylation and intracellular trapping. Further studies are required to determine whether galactose is incorporated into skeletal muscle glycogen to a physiologically meaningful extent.

articles.title: Synergistic modulation of cardiac lipid metabolism by Hedan Pill and Shexiang Baoxin Pill through the peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor α-carnitine palmitoyltransferase 1A axis in experimental heart failure.
articles.authors: Feng Wang, Lixin Wang, Qian Zhang et al.
articles.abstract: Congestive heart failure (CHF) is associated with profound cardiac metabolic remodelling, particularly in lipid utilization. While Hedan Pill and Shexiang Baoxin Pill are traditional Chinese medicines with cardiovascular benefits, their synergistic mechanisms in CHF remain unclear. Network pharmacology and molecular docking were combined with in vivo validation using ApoE-/- mice fed a high-fat diet and subjected to isoproterenol (ISO) treatment. Animals were allocated to seven groups: control, model, Entresto, Hedan Pill, Shexiang Baoxin Pill, Entresto + Hedan Pill, and Entresto + Shexiang Baoxin Pill. Cardiac function, serum lipids, myocardial histopathology, and protein expression of peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor α (PPARα), carnitine palmitoyltransferase 1A (CPT1A) and sterol regulatory element-binding protein 1c (SREBP-1c) were assessed. Network analysis indicated convergence on the PPARα-lipid metabolism pathway, with strong binding affinities between several active compounds and PPARα (≤ -7.0 kcal mol-1). In vivo, Hedan Pill or ShexiangBaoxin Pill alone improved ejection fraction, reduced triglycerides, and alleviated fibrosis and lipid deposition. Compared with Entresto alone, both combination regimens further reduced serum triglycerides and LDL-C, whereas ejection fraction did not differ significantly. Mechanistically, both agents upregulated myocardial PPARα and CPT1A while suppressing SREBP-1c. Hedan Pill and Shexiang Baoxin Pill synergistically improve cardiac lipid metabolic homeostasis through the PPARα-CPT1A axis, thereby protecting against CHF-induced myocardial injury. These findings provide physiological and mechanistic evidence supporting their translational potential as complementary interventions in CHF.

articles.title: Centrality of the periphery: Small muscle mass to bypass O2 transport limitations and maximize the benefits of exercise training in heart failure.
articles.authors: Danilo Iannetta, Fabio Giuseppe Laginestra, Ryan M Broxterman et al.
articles.abstract: Heart failure (HF) is a complex, systemic cardiovascular condition characterized by a severe impairment in O2 transport to skeletal muscle that drives exercise intolerance and reduces quality of life. Although exercise training (ET) is a cornerstone of HF clinical management, patients often exhibit limited improvements in peak oxygen uptake ( V ̇ O 2 peak ) following traditional whole-body, aerobic exercise recruiting a large muscle mass (e.g., cycling). In patients with HF, adaptations within skeletal muscle (e.g., capillarization) exert a proportionally greater influence on changes in V ̇ O 2 peak than adaptations in cardiac performance. In this review, we discuss the mechanisms by which traditional ET prescription may be suboptimal to elicit peripheral adaptations and argue that dynamic exercise recruiting only a small muscle mass (e.g., quadriceps) may be more effective in achieving this goal. Indeed, small muscle mass exercise reduces the cardiovascular restraints imposed by the failing heart, allowing the muscle to reach much greater metabolic rates and to be exposed to much larger degrees of homeostatic perturbations, a key factor triggering adaptations in O2 transport and utilization at the peripheral level. The intent of this review is to discuss the influence of muscle mass on exercise tolerance and adaptations to ET in HF, with the ultimate goal of promoting the integration of small muscle mass exercise into contemporary cardiac rehabilitation programmes.

articles.title: Reappraising Training Exposure in Sports Genomics: A Multidimensional Training Status Framework Prevents Underestimation of Polygenic Effects on Strength-Power Phenotypes.
articles.journal: Journal of strength and conditioning research
articles.authors: Mingrui Wang, Lun Chen, Linghua Yan et al.
articles.abstract: Wang, M, Chen, L, Yan, L, and Wang, J. Reappraising training exposure in sports genomics: A multidimensional training status framework prevents underestimation of polygenic effects on strength-power phenotypes. J Strength Cond Res XX(X): 000-000, 2026-This study examined whether training-exposure representation influences the statistical detectability and effect estimation of the total genotype score (TGS) for strength-power phenotypes. In this cross-sectional study, 187 Han Chinese men (48 national-level or higher-level strength-power athletes and 139 nonathletes) completed body-composition, performance, training-exposure, and genotyping assessments. Thirteen candidate variants were examined: GALNT13 rs10196189, IL6 rs1800795, EPAS1 rs11689011 and rs1867785, AMPD1 rs17602729, ACTN3 rs1815739, AGT rs699, ADRB2 rs1042713, HIF1A rs11549465, IGF1R rs1464430, MCT1 rs1049434, NOS3 rs2070744, and ACE rs4646994. Six variants that passed quality control were integrated into a standardized TGS, and performance was represented by an allometrically adjusted total score of athleticism (TSA). Fourteen linear and logistic models compared training years with multidimensional Training Status. Total genotype score alone was weakly associated with TSA (β = 0.007, p = 0.079; R2 = 0.017). Adding age and training years improved model performance but did not significantly alter the TGS coefficient. By contrast, Training Status increased the TGS coefficient to 0.028 (p < 0.001), explained 51.1% of the variance, and produced larger TGS effects than age- or training-years-based models (all p < 0.001). Discrimination of athlete status improved from area under the curve (AUC) = 0.620 with TGS alone to 0.845 after incorporating Training Status, whereas removing TGS reduced AUC to 0.700. Component-level modeling achieved the highest performance (R2 = 0.618; AUC = 0.876), although these gains did not consistently extend to threshold-dependent classification. Overall, higher-resolution characterization of training exposure reveals polygenic associations partly obscured by duration-based measures.

articles.title: Effects of menstrual cycle on appetite-regulating hormones in response to sprint exercise in physically active females.
articles.journal: Applied physiology, nutrition, and metabolism = Physiologie appliquee, nutrition et metabolisme
articles.authors: Kayoko Kamemoto, Aiko Miyaguchi, Megumi Wanifuchi et al.
articles.abstract: This study investigated whether the effects of sprint exercise on appetite regulation vary across menstrual cycle phases. Eight physically active females completed four trials in a counterbalanced order: exercise (EX) and resting (RE) conditions during both the early follicular phase (FP) and mid-luteal phase (LP). The exercise protocol comprised two sets of eight 6-s maximal sprints, with 30 s of rest between sprints. Blood samples were collected pre-exercise and immediately, 30-min, and 90-min post-exercise to measure glucose, lactate, acylated ghrelin, and total glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1). Subjective appetite was assessed seven times during each trial and free-living energy intake was recorded on each experimental day. Blood lactate were higher in the EX than in the RE immediately and at 30 and 90 min after exercise during both the FP and LP (P ≤ 0.028). Plasma acylated ghrelin was suppressed in the EX compared with the RE at 30 min post-exercise in the LP (P = 0.001, ES = 0.55), whereas plasma total GLP-1 did not differ between phases or trials at any time point. Subjective appetite was suppressed during the EX compared with the RE in both FP and LP at 30 min post-exercise (the FP: P < 0.001, ES = 0.69; the LP: P < 0.001, ES = 1.00). Acute sprint exercise temporarily suppressed subjective appetite during both menstrual phases and acylated ghrelin during the LP; however, no clear menstrual cycle dependent differences in post-exercise appetite regulation were observed (Clinical trial registration ID: UMIN R000059802).

articles.title: Bone biomarker concentrations at baseline and 24 h after resistance and interval running exercise in eumenorrheic females and oral contraceptive users.
articles.journal: Applied physiology, nutrition, and metabolism = Physiologie appliquee, nutrition et metabolisme
articles.authors: Isabel Guisado-Cuadrado, Nuria Romero-Parra, Rocío Cupeiro et al.
articles.abstract: Bone metabolism is influenced by both mechanical loading and the hormonal environment, yet their combined effects on the acute response to exercise remain unclear in premenopausal females. Therefore, this study aimed to examine baseline and 24 h post-exercise concentrations of bone biomarkers following resistance and interval-running exercise, considering menstrual and oral contraceptive (OC) cycle phases. Eight eumenorrheic and 8 OC users performed interval running (8×3 min at 85% maximal aerobic speed), whereas 9 eumenorrheic and 10 OC users completed eccentric-based resistance exercise (10×10 squats at 60% 1RM), according to their trained modality. Trials were conducted in randomized order during the early- and late-follicular phases (EFP, LFP) in eumenorrheic females and withdrawal and active pill phases (WP, APP) in OC users. Blood was sampled at baseline and 24 h post-exercise. Dickkopf-1 (DKK-1) and sclerostin showed Exercise×Time interactions, with lower concentrations 24 h after interval running. Osteocalcin showed Exercise×Phase and Exercise×Time interactions, with lower 24 h concentrations in the endurance- than resistance-trained group and lower concentrations in endurance-trained OC users during APP versus WP. Fibroblast Growth Factor-23 was lower at 24 h, while osteoprotegerin (OPG) was higher in APP than WP. Overall, interval running induced concurrent reductions in DKK-1, sclerostin, and total osteocalcin, indicating a short-term alteration in bone metabolic regulation. The reductions in DKK-1 and sclerostin are compatible with a transient decrease in Wnt pathway inhibition. Osteocalcin and OPG varied across OC phases, highlighting the relevance of considering hormonal status.

articles.title: Chlorella intake combined with short-term high-intensity intermittent training further enhances exercise performance in female lacrosse players: a double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled, crossover trial.
articles.journal: Applied physiology, nutrition, and metabolism = Physiologie appliquee, nutrition et metabolisme
articles.authors: Shumpei Fujie, Ayami Numa, Izumi Tabata et al.
articles.abstract: Lacrosse is a fast-paced field sport that requires aerobic, anaerobic, and sprint performance. Chronic Chlorella intake combined with high-intensity intermittent training (HIIT) enhances aerobic, anaerobic, and sprint performance in untrained young adults. This study aimed to clarify the effects of combining Chlorella intake with short-term HIIT on aerobic, anaerobic, and sprint performance in female lacrosse players. In a double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled crossover trial, twelve female collegiate lacrosse players were enrolled, ten participants completed 3 weeks of HIIT, comprising 7 bouts of running at full speed with a 10-second rest between each bout, 5 days/week. They were orally administered Chlorella (CH) or a placebo (PL) for 3-week in a double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled, crossover design with a 5-week washout period. This study measured the 20-meter shuttle run test (20m SRT) and estimated maximal oxygen uptake (VO2max) as indices of aerobic performance, 50-meter sprint time as an index of sprint performance, and the 30-second Wingate test as an index of anaerobic performance. No significant differences by trial or time point were observed in aerobic (20m SRT and VO2max) or anaerobic performance (Wingate test), including 50-meter sprint time. However, improvements were observed in the HIIT + CH trial for most exercise performance outcomes (P < 0.05), but not in the HIIT + PL trial. These exploratory results suggest that CH intake may improve short-term HIIT-induced changes in exercise performance in female lacrosse players, although the small sample size and short intervention period warrant cautious interpretation.

articles.title: Higher diet costs predict both healthier and less healthy intakes among Canadian adults.
articles.journal: Applied physiology, nutrition, and metabolism = Physiologie appliquee, nutrition et metabolisme
articles.authors: Gabriella Luongo, Valerie Tarasuk, Leah E Cahill et al.
articles.abstract: Diet costs are a predictor of dietary adequacy, however little evidence exists on how diet costs may influence intakes of specific components of the diet. Reported intakes from the first 24-hour dietary recall in the 2015 Canadian Community Health Survey-Nutrition were used to estimate energy density of intakes (kcal/g), and gram weight intakes of total fibre, sodium, fruits, vegetables, processed meats, and caloric beverages, among Canadian adults 19y+. Canadian Consumer Price Index national prices were matched to food sources of intakes to estimate individual 24-hour diet costs (g/day). We examined how diet costs were distributed across the population, and multivariable linear regression models were used to analyze the association between diet costs and dietary intakes important to Canada's Food Guide 2019 and the global burden of diseases. 24-hour diet costs varied significantly across the Canadian population, from an average of $4.90/day in the lowest tertile of diet cost, to $9.26/day and $16.50/day in the moderate and highest tertiles respectively. Differences were found in the sociodemographic makeup of diet cost strata. In the fully-adjusted model controlling for total energy intake (kcal) and sociodemographic factors, for every one dollar increase in diet cost across the whole of the population, Canadians consumed a lower energy density of intakes of 0.02 kcal/g (ptrend <0.0001), higher sodium intakes at 14.54 mg (ptrend <0.0001), and higher vegetables intakes at 3.41g (ptrend <0.0001). Further research and surveillance are needed to examine sociodemographic heterogeneity in how populations may allocate their diet costs differently to achieve nutritious diets.

articles.title: Corrigendum to "Nutritional Value Score Rates Foods Based on Nutrient Density and Noncommunicable Disease Prevention" [The Journal of Nutrition. 2026;156(5):101443].
Corn Syrup Solids in Infant Formula and Child Health Outcomes: A Systematic Review.
articles.authors: Ying Liao, Shasha Cui, Kevin Fiscella et al.
articles.abstract: CONTEXT: The potential impact of corn syrup solids (CSSs) in infant formula on long-term child health outcomes is a critical area of investigation, informing nutritional guidelines and parental choices. OBJECTIVE: This systematic review aimed to investigate the effects of CSSs in infant formula on various child health outcomes. DATA SOURCES: Following PRISMA guidelines, our PROSPERO-registered protocol (CRD420261306977) guided a comprehensive search of PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library, completed on January 23, 2026. DATA EXTRACTION: From 150 identified studies, titles and abstracts were screened, followed by full-text review. Data from eligible studies were extracted independently in duplicate, and study quality and risk of bias were assessed. DATA ANALYSIS: We extracted data from 5 observational and 2 controlled interventional studies. Two studies reported a higher early childhood obesity risk in children fed CSS-containing formula. Other findings included increased food fussiness, decreased food enjoyment, frequent sweet intake, and gut microbiota changes (depleted Bifidobacteriaceae, enriched Lachnospiraceae). Short-term postprandial differences in plasma metabolites and gastric acidity were also noted. Four studies had low risk of bias, 3 had moderate risk. CONCLUSIONS: This systematic review suggests that CSS-containing formula intake during infancy may be associated with altered eating behaviors, gut microbiota changes, acute metabolic responses, and childhood obesity. Future well-designed randomized controlled trials (RCTs) are needed to elucidate these connections. Limitations include a scarcity of robust RCTs, imprecise exposure data, and exclusion of non-English studies. SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: PROSPERO registration No. [CRD420261306977].

articles.title: Dietary Sugar Intake and Risk of Cognitive Disorders: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.authors: Zilan Chen, Yuqi Pang, Ye Ju et al.
articles.abstract: CONTEXT: Although prior studies have linked excessive dietary sugar intake to adverse cognitive outcomes, the findings of individual studies remain inconsistent, and there is a lack of synthesis. OBJECTIVE: The objective of this study was to comprehensively examine the association between dietary sugar intake and risk of cognitive disorders. DATA SOURCES: The Cochrane, Embase, PubMed, ScienceDirect, and Web of Science databases were searched from inception to December 2025. DATA EXTRACTION: Prospective cohort, nested case-control or case-cohort studies evaluating the association of dietary total sugar or its subtypes with the risk of cognitive disorders, including cognitive impairment and dementia (including Alzheimer's disease), in adults were reviewed. Details of the studies and main outcomes were extracted independently by 2 reviewers. DATA ANALYSIS: Among 2171 records screened, 10 prospective cohort studies comprising 12 cohorts and 257 761 participants were included. The number of cohorts and participants for each exposure was as follows: total sugar: 5 (N = 200 812); sugar-sweetened beverages: 9 (N = 214 084); fruit juice: 2 (N = 194 847); fructose: 4 (N = 197 082); sucrose: 3 (N = 194 928); lactose: 3 (N = 194 928); maltose: 3 (N = 194 928); glucose: 3 (N = 194 928). Meta-analysis indicated that individuals with the highest total sugar intake were at a higher risk of cognitive disorders compared with those with the lowest intake (hazard ratio = 1.23, 95% CI = 1.10-1.38, low certainty). No significant associations were observed for any specific sugar subtypes examined, with certainty of evidence ranging from low to very low. CONCLUSIONS: The present review suggests that higher total sugar intake may be associated with an increased risk of cognitive disorders. In contrast, the current evidence does not support a clear association between specific sugar subtypes and cognitive disorders. Future studies should prioritize clarifying the dose-response relationship between total sugar intake and cognitive disorders. SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: PROSPERO registration No. CRD42025640308.

articles.title: Effects of Resveratrol Supplementation on Exercise-Induced Muscle Damage: A Narrative Review.
articles.authors: Sheng-Lei Yang, Guang-Xin Wang, Yan-Yuan Du et al.
articles.abstract: Exercise-induced muscle damage (EIMD) is a common consequence of high-intensity or unfamiliar physical activity and can lead to muscle soreness, inflammation, oxidative stress, and temporary loss of muscle function. Although various interventions have been explored to alleviate EIMD, resveratrol (RES), a natural polyphenolic compound found in grapes, berries, and other plants, has attracted attention due to its potential antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties. This review aims to explore the effects of RES on EIMD in terms of its impact on muscle recovery, inflammation, and oxidative stress markers. This review synthesizes the results of preclinical and clinical studies and highlights the timing, dosage, and efficacy of exercise-associated RES. Although the results are promising, with several studies reporting reduced muscle damage and improved recovery, inconsistencies in RES administration timing, dosage, and bioavailability require further investigation. Understanding these factors is critical to optimizing the therapeutic potential of RES in both the exercise and clinical settings. Finally, the review summarizes the potential of RES as a safe and effective intervention for EIMD and implications for future research.
